title: Exponential backpressure and headroom microbatch thresholds for surge QPS
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS bursts we observe runaway microbatch growth that maximizes throughput at the cost of long tail latency and periodic OOMs due to KV cache churn and GPU memory fragmentation. Prior mitigations (static microbatch ceilings) either sacrifice throughput on normal traffic or fail to prevent latency spikes during surges.

Objective: Implement an adaptive admission and backpressure system that enforces exponential soft watermarks for microbatch size and a conservative hard headroom reserve for KV cache + model state. The feature should: (1) keep 99.9th percentile latency within SLO during surges, (2) avoid OOMs by maintaining safe GPU headroom, (3) preserve throughput for cache-warm traffic where possible, and (4) be observable and togglable for gradual rollout.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Default exponential backpressure policy is enabled in runtime config. 2) Under synthetic burst test (10x baseline QPS for 60s) 99.9p latency < 4x baseline and no GPU OOMs. 3) KV cache eviction rate and reuse hit-rate dashboards show reduced thrashing compared to baseline. 4) Canary rollout to 5% nodes with automated rollback if error rate > 1% or OOMs occur.
tasks: Design exponential backpressure curve and parameters (alpha/beta/time constants)
Implement admission controller that applies per-worker token-bucket + dynamic watermarking
Integrate headroom reservation accounting for KV cache + model peaks
Add request prioritization: prefer cache-hit warm prefixes when shaping
Expose runtime flags and per-node metrics (current watermark, queue depth, headroom)
Create synthetic workload harness and dashboard for surge tests
Run cluster canary and analyze metrics, iterate on parameters
Document rollout, failure modes, and tuning guide in Confluence
progress_updates: 2026-03-12: Ticket created after repeated incidents on 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-11 where heavy QPS spikes caused KV eviction storms and sporadic OOMs in us-west-2 runtime pool.
2026-03-13: Design review with SRE and Runtime leads. Agreed on exponential soft-watermark + hard reserve approach. Key constraint: minimal added per-request latency when under normal load.

2026-03-14: Initial prototype of admission controller merged to feature/exp-backpressure branch (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3126). Prototype implements token-bucket gating and per-worker dynamic watermark. Microbench harness added under ci/bench/surge_sim.

2026-03-14: Ran local node simulation with 10k qps synthetic traffic. Results: tail latency improvement ~35% vs static ceiling; observed headroom accounting prevented OOMs in 3/3 runs. Need to tune alpha to reduce throughput loss for cache-warm traffic.
2026-03-14: Noted edge case where long-running streaming requests can hold KV cache segments and reduce effective headroom. Added task to detect streaming-heavy nodes and apply per-stream quotas.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Chose exponential soft watermark rather than linear to avoid repeated oscillation at high QPS — exponential curve provides smoother throttling as load grows quickly.

We prefer delaying (backpressure/admission) over dropping to preserve user experience; however, in extreme overload we will implement an emergency drop policy for un-authenticated or low-priority requests to protect SLOs.

Headroom reserve size trade-off: larger reserve reduces OOM risk but reduces achievable throughput. Default reserve set to 12% of GPU memory plus 256MB per active KV partition as a conservative starting point; will tune based on canary data.

Prioritization: favor requests with high KV cache hit probability to maximize effective throughput. Trade-off: could disadvantage cold traffic; mitigations include short-lived priority boosts for newly-seen prefixes.
experiments_and_results: Synthetic surge test (baseline 1k QPS -> 10k QPS for 60s): prototype reduced 99.9p latency from 1.9s to 0.9s on a 80-token average workload, throughput delta -12% vs baseline static ceiling.
KV cache churn metric (evictions/min) reduced by ~48% in simulation runs when prioritization by predicted cache-hit was enabled.
Memory safety: previously observed OOMs in 2 of 5 stress runs are now 0 of 10 when headroom accounting is active.
Failure mode found: bursts with many long-streamed tokens still caused high memory residency; mitigation: per-stream soft quota and immediate KV segment release after stream completion.
implementation_notes: Admission controller is implemented as a library module (runtime/pkg/admit) exposing: Evaluate(request_meta) -> Admit/Delay/Drop and current watermark metadata.
Watermark state stored in per-worker atomic struct; aggregated via existing node exporter metrics with new metrics: runtime_backpressure_watermark, runtime_headroom_bytes, runtime_admit_denied_count.
KV cache accounting extended to report estimated transient footprint per-request so headroom calc can include in-flight allocations.
Added feature flag 'runtime.exp_backpressure' with rollout gating and per-cluster parameter overrides.

PR references: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3126 (prototype), github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3140 (metrics & feature flag), github.com/redwood-inference/ci/pull/893 (surge harness)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Too-aggressive backpressure reduces throughput for normal traffic. Mitigation: conservative default params, canary rollout and automated rollback if throughput drops > 20% for non-surge intervals.

Risk: Incorrect headroom calc underestimates transient allocations from third-party kernels. Mitigation: add safety multiplier and runtime validation check that triggers circuit-breaker if actual free memory < reserved * 0.85.
Risk: Prioritization causes starvation for cold customers. Mitigation: implement aging-based priority increases and crow-based fairness boosting after N seconds in queue.
Risk: UX impact from increased observed latency for certain requests. Mitigation: expose per-route shaping labels and allow customers to opt-in to high-throughput, low-latency tiering in Console.
next_steps: Tune alpha/beta parameters from canary telemetry and run 24h continuous surge simulations.
Implement per-stream soft quota and immediate KV release path, add unit/integration tests.
Schedule canary rollout to 5% then 20% clusters with close SRE monitoring dashboards and automated rollback hooks.
Update runbook and incident playbook with new backpressure signals and remediation steps.
Gather PM/Design feedback on customer-visible rate-limit messaging and incorporate into Console alerts.
